newsitem.title: HUNGARY: CSFB RATES PICK "BUY", SEES UNDERVALUED.
newsitem.headline: CSFB RATES PICK "BUY", SEES UNDERVALUED.

text.p: Cs First Boston (CSFB) rated Hungarian meat food processor Pick Rt shares as "buy" saying the stocks are undervalued and the group has a highly desirable mix of export growth and exposure to domestic consumption.
Pick, releasing its consolidated January-September results this morning, said its profits and sales were above both last year's figure and this year's nine-month target.

Still, Pick, once viewed as one of the best quality and most desirable stocks on the Budapest bourse, has been an afterthought in this year's exporter and construction-based market rally, CSFB's analyst Spencer Jakab said in an update.

Pick has lagged behind the market with a 12 percent appreciation in 1996 against an over 100 percent rise in dollar terms of the BUX index so far, Jakab said, adding the stocks do not deserve to trade at a discount to the market.
The analyst cited several reasons to back his opinion.
"Pick is an anomaly in the sense that it derives the bulk of its revenues from the sale of a premium product, yet it has been affected less than its Hungarian peer group by austerity," Jakab said.

Thus the share was an austerity-proof consumer stock, he said, adding its earnings per share grew by 37.5 percent in 1995, when due to the country's austerity package launched in March 1995, real wages dropped by around 11 percent.

Furthermore, if the domestic economy were to slide back into recession Pick would face limited direct competition, low cyclicality of earnings and limited demand downside, because it is a food company essentially with a premium product.
Pick is also well positioned to expand within Hungary's food-processing sector, Jakab said.
"As the industry continues to suffer from liquidity problems and low capacity utilisation, Pick is one of the few companies in a position to expand," the analyst said.
"Pick is already more or less vertically integrated, the company's strategic position could be enhanced by acquiring companies which rely on the same distribution channels."
On the Budapest Stock Exchange Pick shares closed at 7,100 forints, up 50.
